To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
single-bit control flow error vulnerabilities exist in x86-based systems, and these vulnerabilities can be exploited by an adversary to gain control over the system.

(a) the Intel x86 processor architecture is vulnerable to single-bit control flow attacks; (b) the vulnerabilities can lead to security violations; (c) the vulnerabilities can be reduced using a new encoding scheme; and (d) the vulnerabilities are not caused by the use of conditional branch instructions.

(a) single-bit control flow faults in the authentication section of two Internet server applications can result in serious security vulnerabilities; (b) the security vulnerabilities are caused by the fact that conditional branch instructions in the x86 are a minimum of Hamming distance 1 apart; and (c) a new encoding scheme can reduce or eliminate the security vulnerabilities.

the problem of security vulnerabilities caused in the Intel x86 processor architecture by single-bit control flow error injection into the authentication sections of applications.
the security of software systems and the security implications of single-bit control flow error.
the problem of single-bit control flow error detection and its impact on security.

single-bit control flow faults are a serious threat to security.
, in the Intel x86 processor, single-bit control errors in the authentication section of targeted applications are a significant security concern.
single-bit control flow error detection is an essential component in the design of secure applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results show that single-bit control flow error injection is a viable approach to the study of control flow errors in software.

the study shows that the Intel x86 processor architecture has serious security vulnerabilities that are caused by single-bit control flow faults, and that these vulnerabilities are not eliminated even by the latest Intel processors (Pentium 4 and Xeon).

, for the x86 architecture: (1) a single-bit control flow error can result in a significant security vulnerability (a system security vulnerability in approximately 1-2%, and a transient window of security vulnerability in approximately one out of every two crash failures); (2) the security vulnerabilities caused by a single-bit control error are not restricted to the application code that was modified, but can also affect other applications running in the system; (3) the security vulnerabilities are not restricted to a single user
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to achieve high security, software developers should consider the effects of single-bit errors on the control flow of their software.
, in order to ensure security, it is not sufficient to ensure that an application does not contain any single-bit control flow error in its security-critical sections.
the security of a system can be compromised by a small number of bit errors.
